reference.name: VanHecken2020
reference.title: Relative Bioavailability of Enalapril Administered as Orodispersible Minitablets in Healthy Adults.
reference.abstract: The angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor enalapril is commonly used to treat chronic heart failure in children. Because some children are unable to swallow capsules or tablets, a new, age-appropriate, orodispersible minitablet (ODMT) containing 1 mg of enalapril was developed within the EU-funded LENA (Labeling of Enalapril from Neonates up to Adolescents) consortium. In order to support the clinical evaluation of this new formulation in children, a relative bioavailability study was performed in healthy adults, comparing the bioavailability of enalapril in the ODMT with that of a reference product (RP) Renitec, a registered standard enalapril tablet formulation. In this open-label, randomized 3-way crossover study, 24 healthy subjects received a 10-mg enalapril dose administered as (1) 2 × 5-mg tablets of the RP swallowed with water, (2) 10 × 1-mg ODMT swallowed with water, and (3) 10 × 1 mg ODMT dispersed on the tongue. descriptions.text: The study involved 24 healthy nonsmokers, consisting of 11 nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding female and 13 male volunteers between 18 and 55 years old with body mass index between 18.5 and 30 kg/m^2
After an overnight fast, the study subjects were administered a 10-mg enalapril maleate oral dose on 3 occasions, separated by at least 1 week of washout
Treatment A: 2 × 5-mg tablets of the RP swallowed with 240 mL of water
Treatment B: 10 × 1-mg ODMT, swallowed with 240 mL of water
Treatment C: 10 × 1-mg ODMT, dispersed on the tongue following wetting of the mouth with 20 mL of water, followed by administration of 220 mL of water at 1 hour postdose
blood samples were obtained for the determination of enalapril and enalaprilat at predose and at 10, 20, 30, 45 minutes and 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 24, 36, and 48 hours

Twenty-three subjects successfully completed all 3 periods of the study. One subject had a predose positive drug screen for tetrahydrocannabinol in study period 2 and therefore did not receive treatment A; received only the 2 ODMT treatments
